title: Crisis Intervention Strategies
tagline: Steady hands for the worst hours.
welcome: In a crisis, a young person borrows your calm. This course builds that calm into skill, so you can act decisively when minutes matter.
vignette: At 9 p.m. a text arrives from a sixteen-year-old client: 'I can't do this anymore.' Three words, no name, no location. The counselor's training activates: assess, stabilize, mobilize. This course is what makes those verbs reliable.
vignette_attr: An after-hours crisis contact, drawn from practice
description: A rigorous training in crisis theory and intervention with children and adolescents: risk and suicide assessment, de-escalation and stabilization, safety planning, mobilizing families and schools, postvention, and the counselor's own regulation under pressure.
questions: How do I assess lethal risk with a minor, clearly and kindly?
What stabilizes a dysregulated young person in the room?
Who must be mobilized, and how do I keep the client's trust?
importance: Youth suicide and crisis presentations are rising; counselors are first responders
Crisis competence is the most scrutinized skill in child practice
A good crisis response can end a chain of tragedy permanently
misconceptions: that asking about suicide plants the idea, when asking directly is protective
that crisis work is improvisation, when it is highly structured and trainable
figures: whose collaborative assessment and stabilization model saved lives
outcomes: You will assess suicide and harm risk with validated, collaborative methods.
You will use regulation and grounding to bring a crisis down in the room.
You will co-author safety plans a young person will actually use.
You will engage family, school, and care with clarity and consent.
Respond after a death or traumatic event
You will apply postvention and psychological first aid.
You will keep your own physiology and judgment steady.
modules: The Nature of Crisis in Young People
A clear model turns alarm into method.
Assessment is a conversation, not a checklist.
Safety Planning and Lethal Means Counseling
A good plan is specific, personal, and rehearsed.
The child is held by a system; we activate it.
Postvention is prevention for the next crisis.
Your steadiness is the intervention; we train it deliberately.
practicum: Practice is simulated at full intensity.
assessment: Assessment tests performance under simulated pressure.
tips: Rehearse your first five minutes until automatic
Memorize your local crisis and referral pathways
Debrief every crisis; never carry one alone
integration: Crisis competence crowns your clinical training and is assumed in internship and practice.
faith: We stand with young people in their darkest hour as witnesses of hope that is disciplined, not sentimental.
closing: May your calm be a shelter, and may no young person face their worst hour alone.
